title.value: Bayesian Latent Multi-State Modeling for Non-Equidistant Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
title.justification: The title directly refers to the core subject of the paper, which is modeling electronic health records data in a Bayesian framework, considering non-equidistant observation times.
title.quote: # Bayesian Latent Multi-State Modeling for Non-Equidistant Longitudinal Electronic Health Records

analysis.description: The paper develops a Bayesian continuous-time hidden Markov model (CTHMM) to study longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), focusing on handling non-equidistant data. It involves Bayesian inference using MCMC, with applications to a COPD cohort.

type.justification: The paper is primarily focused on developing a theoretical framework rather than conducting experiments or empirical assessments.
type.quote: The Bayesian approach has not been widely used for the analysis of such data due to computational scale and complexity, and yet it provides a more complete representation of inferential uncertainty.

name.justification: The paper is centered around modeling healthcare data, particularly longitudinal EHRs, in a Bayesian framework.
name.quote: Large amounts of longitudinal health records are now available for dynamic monitoring of the underlying processes governing the observations.

name.justification: The paper uses a Bayesian approach for modeling and inference.
name.quote: We focus on Bayesian inference for the model: this is facilitated by an expectation-maximization algorithm and Markov chain Monte Carlo methods.

name.justification: The paper develops a continuous-time hidden Markov model (HMM) for data analysis.
name.quote: We develop a continuous-time hidden Markov model to analyze longitudinal data accounting for irregular visits and different types of observations.

name.justification: The paper introduces a continuous-time hidden Markov model as the core contribution.
name.quote: We develop a continuous-time hidden Markov model to analyze longitudinal data accounting for irregular visits and different types of observations.

is_contributed.justification: The CTHMM model is a key development presented in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: In this paper, we develop a continuous-time hidden Markov model (CTHMM) and an observation generalized linear model (GLM) to draw inference in a fully Bayesian setting.

is_executed.justification: The paper does not specifically mention the execution platform, whether CPU or GPU.
is_executed.quote: Simulation studies demonstrate that these approaches can be implemented efficiently for large data sets in a fully Bayesian setting.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares the developed model with other models in simulation studies.
is_compared.quote: We compare our EM method based on exact continuous time formulation with their discrete approximation EM algorithm.

referenced_paper_title.value: A Bayesian approach to multistate hidden Markov models: Application to dementia progression
referenced_paper_title.justification: The cited paper is used as a reference for Bayesian approaches to hidden Markov models.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Recently, Williams et al. (2019) constructed a Bayesian continuous-time HMM to study dementia progression, using restrictions on the parameter space to identify the parameters in the HMM.

name.justification: The dataset consists of COPD patients over 65 years old, used for analysis in the study.
name.quote: In this application, we apply our method to the data described in Section 1.1. The data set consists of 33,876 COPD patients over 65 years old.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The dataset is related to the study conducted on hospital readmissions, and the paper by Verma is relevant to this dataset.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Verma, A. (2015). Hospital Readmissions: Prediction and Inference. PhD thesis, McGill University.

name.justification: These datasets are generated for model testing and validation as described in the simulation study sections.
name.quote: In our simulation we observed performance improvement when T is increased.

referenced_paper_title.value: Statistical inference for discretely observed Markov jump processes
referenced_paper_title.justification: The reference paper provides background on statistical inference methods useful for analyzing the simulated data in this study.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Bladt, M. and Sørensen, M. (2005). Statistical inference for discretely observed Markov jump processes.

name.justification: The paper mentions the development of an R package to implement the proposed methods.
name.quote: The package cthmmglm to implement the proposed EM algorithm and MCMC is provided along with the instruction to install the package and run the example data.
